part.material_note: High-carbon chromium bearing steel (equivalent BS 970:1991 535A99). Normally used in hardened and ground condition for wear-resistant applications.

Chamfer appears on both ends in the model but callout points to one end only. Change to: 2x 0.5 x 45 degrees to avoid ambiguity.
Recommended values: OD Ra <= 0.4 um, ID Ra <= 0.8 um, faces Ra <= 1.6 um.

drawing_clarifications.topic: Concentricity / runout between ID and OD not defined

Add: Remove all burrs, No sharp edges, No grinding burns or decarburization.

ID_pre_HT_mm.note: Do not finish bore before hardening — thin wall may distort during quench

chamfer_pre_HT_mm.note: Pre-machine chamfers to reduce quench-crack risk

raw_material.rationale: Solid round bar preferred over seamless tube for only 4 pieces. Annealed condition required for soft machining stage.
requirements: Bar free from seams, cracks, excessive decarburization and bending
Do not mix different EN31 heat-treatment batches

recommended_machine.primary: CNC turn-mill or Swiss-type CNC with sub-spindle and bar feeder
recommended_machine.rationale: Both ID and OD can be produced in one clamping for best concentricity. Bar feeder enables unmanned production of 4 pieces.

machining_sequence_principle.rough_order: ID first, then OD — in the same collet clamping
machining_sequence_principle.finish_order: Semi-finish ID then finish-grind OD using ID as datum then final-hone ID
reason_for_ID_first: At O10 mm starting bar the wall after O5 mm drilling is ~2.50 mm — nearly twice the finished 1.34 mm wall
Thicker wall reduces drill vibration, bore wandering, ovality and unequal wall thickness
Machining OD and ID in one setup aligns their axes
Finishing OD before drilling produces only ~1.35 mm wall during subsequent boring — high risk of distortion and eccentricity
reason_for_ID_datum_in_finish: Finished bore provides precise geometric reference for mandrel mounting
OD ground to the bore axis gives best ID-to-OD concentricity
Final honing after OD grinding corrects any small bore deformation from mandrel clamping

machining_sequence_comparison.summary: ID-first is the best approach for both rough machining and finish grinding of this thin-wall dowel.

comparison_table.reason: When OD is turned to ~O8 mm first, wall after subsequent O5 mm drilling is only ~1.35 mm. This thin wall vibrates, deforms under collet pressure, causes bore wandering, ovality and heat-induced bore expansion during drilling.
Wall at time of drilling is ~2.50 mm (full O10 bar). Provides nearly twice the rigidity. Machining both ID and OD in one collet clamping aligns their axes.

comparison_table.sequence: Rough ID then rough OD then HT then finish ID then finish OD
comparison_table.reason: Separates soft-machining from precision finishing. Heat treatment distortion is dealt with during the grinding stages.

comparison_table.sequence: Rough ID then rough OD then HT then semi-finish ID then finish OD then final-hone ID
comparison_table.reason: Semi-finishing ID first gives a reference for mandrel mounting. Grinding OD to the bore axis maximises concentricity. Final hone corrects any bore deformation from mandrel pressure.

why_OD_first_fails.calculation: (8.00 - 5.30) / 2 = 1.35 mm wall when OD already turned to O8
risks: Bore vibration and wandering during drilling
Ovality from thin wall under collet pressure
Loss of concentricity between ID and OD

why_ID_first_is_better.calculation: (10.00 - 5.00) / 2 = 2.50 mm wall when drilling from full O10 bar
benefits: Both rough ID and OD axes aligned in same clamping

step_1.purpose: Provides accurate bore for mandrel location during OD grinding

step_2.mandrel_type: Close-fitting solid arbor with axial clamping or low-pressure segmented mandrel
step_2.mandrel_warning: Do not use strongly expanding mandrel — 1.34 mm wall will distort

step_3.purpose: Corrects any small bore deformation caused by mandrel pressure during OD grinding

what_not_to_do: Do not finish ID to O5.30-5.32 then aggressively rough-turn OD from O10 to O8 — distorts bore
Do not heat treat after finishing either ID or OD — heat treatment changes both dimensions
Do not use heavy expanding mandrel for OD grinding — 1.34 mm wall deforms under expansion pressure
machining_sequence_comparison.recommended_flow: Face -> Drill ID -> Rough bore ID -> Rough-turn OD in same setup -> Part off and face -> Heat treatment -> Semi-finish ID -> Finish-grind OD using ID as datum -> Final-hone ID -> Chamfer and inspect

process_sequence.name: Incoming material inspection
checks: EN31 material certificate — verify heat number
Do not mix EN31 batches of different heat-treatment history

process_sequence.name: Blank preparation (optional when bar-fed CNC used)
actions: Cut blank to O10 x 34 mm
Remove large saw burrs before loading into CNC
process_sequence.note: This operation can be skipped when machining directly from a bar-fed CNC lathe

process_sequence.name: CNC turning — first side
process_sequence.machine: CNC turn-mill or Swiss CNC with sub-spindle
process_sequence.workholding: O10 mm precision collet — not conventional three-jaw chuck
sequence: Face first end
Spot-drill accurately on spindle centre — critical for equal wall thickness
Drill through with ~O5.0 mm through-coolant carbide drill (L/D ratio ~6:1)
Lightly bore ID to correct drill runout
Rough-turn OD in same clamping without removing part
Machine first preliminary chamfer ~0.35-0.40 x 45 degrees
Part off or transfer to sub-spindle

pre_HT_targets.note: Do not finish ID to O5.30 before hardening

drilling_O5mm.pecking: Only when chip evacuation requires it

cutting_parameters_annealed_EN31.spindle_speed_note: For O10 mm OD stock, typical OD turning rpm ~3800-5000 subject to machine limits

process_sequence.name: CNC turning — second side
process_sequence.workholding: Full-contact collet — low clamping pressure (~1.5 mm wall at this stage)
sequence: Face second end
Establish pre-HT length 30.30-30.40 mm
Machine second preliminary chamfer ~0.35-0.40 x 45 degrees
Lightly deburr ID edge
Do not add large internal chamfer unless shown on drawing

process_sequence.name: Pre-heat-treatment inspection
checks: Complete burr removal — no loose material in bore
No eccentric drilling — measure wall variation
Bore-to-OD runout <= 0.05 mm recommended — reduces final grinding problems
Wash parts thoroughly — oil and coolant residue must not enter furnace

process_sequence.name: Heat treatment
process_sequence.specification: Through harden and temper EN31 to 58-62 HRC (subject to design approval)

typical_process.method: Vacuum heat treatment preferred — avoids scale and decarburization
typical_process.austenitising_temp_C: 830-850 (confirm with heat-treatment department and material certificate)
typical_process.tempering: Low-temperature temper to achieve target hardness

precautions: Do not pack thin sleeves tightly together
Use vacuum or protective atmosphere — no scale or decarburization
Process one hardness test coupon with the batch
Record batch number and furnace chart
post_HT_inspection: Crack inspection — visual and magnetic particle if load-critical
process_sequence.note: Exact temperature, soaking time and quenching method must be established by heat-treatment department based on material certificate, furnace load, section thickness, required hardness and distortion trials

process_sequence.name: Face grinding
process_sequence.machine: CNC surface grinder with fixture, or double-disc grinder
actions: Grind both faces to length 30.00 +/- 0.05 mm
Ensure faces are square to part axis

process_sequence.name: Internal grinding and honing
process_sequence.machine: CNC internal grinder then precision honing machine
sequence: Internal-grind bore to ~O5.305-5.308 mm
Hone to O5.310 mm production target
Check bore taper over full 30 mm length — GO gauge must pass full length
Confirm roundness
process_sequence.note: Finish bore first — it becomes the datum reference for OD grinding

process_sequence.name: OD cylindrical grinding
process_sequence.machine: CNC cylindrical grinder with CBN wheel suitable for hardened EN31

workholding.type: Precision low-force mandrel referenced from finished bore
workholding.mandrel_size_mm: O5.302-5.306 (close fit, not interference — wall is only ~1.34 mm)
workholding.warning: Do not use heavy expanding mandrel — risk of bore distortion and wall deformation

sequence: Multiple light finishing passes
Adequate coolant flow
Two or three spark-out passes
No blueing or grinding burns
Inspect at both ends and at centre

process_sequence.name: Final honing of ID
process_sequence.action: Lightly hone bore to O5.310 +/- 0.005 mm — corrects any small bore deformation from mandrel during OD grinding

process_sequence.name: Final chamfering
process_sequence.requirement: 2x 0.5 x 45 degrees external chamfers, both ends
machine_options: CNC cylindrical grinder with profile wheel
Hard-turning CNC lathe with CBN insert
notes: Part is hardened — standard carbide wears rapidly. Prefer CBN tooling or grinding.
Only lightly deburr internal bore edges — do not create unapproved large internal chamfer

process_sequence.name: Deburring, cleaning and preservation
process_sequence.caution: Do not use aggressive polishing that could reduce OD below O7.98 mm

process_sequence.name: Final inspection — 100% all features
process_sequence.note: Measure all features after parts stabilise at 20 deg C — thermal expansion is significant relative to 20 um tolerance band

inspection_plan.equipment: 0.001 mm outside micrometer or air gauge
inspection_plan.positions: Near end-1, centre, near end-2; two angular directions at each — detects taper and ovality

inspection_plan.equipment: Air gauge or three-point bore micrometer
inspection_plan.positions: Both ends and centre; check taper and roundness

inspection_plan.equipment: Visual; MPI if safety- or load-critical
Calculated from measured OD and ID — (OD minus ID) / 2
inspection_plan.note: Must be >= 1.33 mm at all measurement positions

CNC_turning_stage.purpose: Accurate drill location on spindle centre
Bore correction and concentricity after drilling

grinding_stage.purpose: Workholding for OD grinding — referenced from finished bore
Final chamfers if hard-turning route selected

machine_allocation.equipment: CNC turn-mill or Swiss CNC with sub-spindle
Sub-spindle or rechucking in bored soft collet

machine_allocation.in_house: subcontract if no suitable vacuum furnace

machine_allocation.equipment: CNC surface grinder or double-disc grinder
CNC cylindrical grinder with CBN wheel
CNC grinder with profile wheel or hard-turning with CBN insert
Air gauges, bore micrometer, roundness tester, surface tester

route_summary_hardened: Incoming inspection -> Saw blank O10x34 mm -> CNC: face, spot-drill, drill ID O5.0, rough-bore ID to O5.10-5.15, rough-turn OD to O8.15-8.20 in same clamping, preliminary chamfer, part-off -> Second-op: face to length 30.30-30.40, second chamfer, deburr -> Pre-HT inspection (HOLD) -> Through-harden to 58-62 HRC in vacuum -> Post-HT inspection -> Face-grind to 30.00+/-0.05 -> Internal-grind + hone ID to O5.310+/-0.005 -> OD cylindrical-grind on precision mandrel to O7.990+/-0.005 -> Final-hone ID to correct mandrel deformation -> Finish chamfers 2x0.5x45 degrees -> Deburr, clean, preserve -> 100% final inspection
route_summary_soft_no_HT: Incoming inspection -> Saw blank O10x34 mm -> CNC: face, spot-drill, drill O5.0, bore ID to ~O5.30-5.31 by precision boring or reaming -> Turn OD to ~O8.01 -> Part-off and reverse -> Face to 30.00 mm -> Both 0.5x45 degree chamfers -> Cylindrical-grind OD to O7.990+/-0.005 mm -> Deburr, clean, inspect. Note: Does not provide wear resistance expected from EN31 dowel. Recommended only if designer confirms no hardening required.

recommended_final_specification.length: 30.0 mm (drawing general tolerance +/- 0.2 mm; production target 30.00 +/- 0.05 mm)
recommended_final_specification.runout: ID total runout <= 0.02 mm relative to OD axis (datum A)
